summary: Unexpected postpaid charge on staging API key during canary model rollout - metering attributed to production org
environment: staging:us-east (customer staging key) / prod:us-east (customer prod org)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a $1,250 postpaid charge invoiced to their production org after a canary rollout. The customer uses a dedicated account with separate staging API keys which they expect to be covered by an internal sandbox allowance. BrightCart says the usage shows against their production org (parent) rather than the staging subaccount and that charges appeared overnight (billing date 2026-03-13).

Impact:
- Customer received an unexpected invoice charge of $1,250 for what they claim was low-traffic staging tests.
- Billing alerts triggered for the production org, causing PagerDuty alerts and SLA noise.
- Customer paused all deployments until attribution is resolved.

Environment:
- Dedicated account on us-east-1.
- Canary rollout performed from staging key associated with org: brightcart-staging (subaccount id: sb-87623).
- Production org: brightcart-prod (org id: org-11911).

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC: customer initiated canary rollout from staging key (sb-87623) to test redwood-rlhf-1.2b with a small percentage of traffic.
2) 2026-03-12 22:05–23:30 UTC: steady stream of canary requests (hundreds) with long-context generation.
3) 2026-03-13 03:05 UTC: internal metering batch job ran and aggregated per-hour usage for both orgs and persisted to billing table.
4) 2026-03-13 04:20 UTC: billing job attributed aggregated tokens from sb-87623 to parent org org-11911 and generated a charge.
5) 2026-03-13 08:30 UTC: BrightCart received invoice notification and opened support ticket.

Expected behavior:
- Usage originating from staging API key (sb-87623) should be billed to the staging subaccount and reflect sandbox allowances.

Actual behavior:
- Metering pipeline appears to have collapsed subaccount attribution, assigning tokens to the parent production org, generating an unexpected charge.

Logs / Evidence provided by customer:
- Customer attached a CSV of API request IDs and timestamps (redacted) showing requests tied to sb-87623.
- Billing invoice (PDF) showing $1,250 charge to brightcart-prod for 2026-03-13.

Customer notes:
- They temporarily disabled canary after seeing invoices.
- They request a reversal/credit for the charge and confirmation of fix.

investigation: Investigation summary: Reproduced failure in staging using metering nightly snapshot. Root cause traced to merge in PR #981 (metering service) where late-aggregation join omitted 'subaccount_id' for requests that used staging API keys with a nonstandard metadata header. The late-aggregation path (runs in worker 'billing-aggregator-v2') falls back to 'owner_org' if subaccount_id is null. A regression test gap allowed this. Evidence: query logs (billing-db) show tokens originally tagged with sb-87623, but final billing_row entries show org-11911. Observed similar null propagation for two other subaccounts but only BrightCart crossed billing threshold. Related artifacts: slack thread #billing-ops (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C07BILL/12345), GH PR 981, billing DB query ids qb-7741, qb-7742.
resolution:
Resolution summary: 1) Immediate: disabled nightly aggregation job for the affected window and re-ran reconciliation script with corrected join logic to preserve subaccount_id. 2) Billing: issued a $1,250 credit memo to brightcart-prod and offered immediate refund; customer selected credit memo (will appear on next invoice). 3) Engineering: merged hotfix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/987) to ensure subaccount_id is never overwritten with null in late-aggregation; added regression tests covering staging key flow. 4) Follow-up actions: postmortem scheduled, add monitoring alert on sudden parent-org charge spikes, add canary for metering aggregation.

Notes for CS ops: Credit memo number CM-2026-317 applied to org-11911; billing asked to notify customer once credit posts. Engineering estimate for hotfix to reach prod: 6 hours (completed 2026-03-14 04:30 UTC). Postmortem (internal) due 2026-03-21.
